content.title: About
content.content: Cracker chips are crunchy snack sticks made from wheat flour, vegetable oil, and seasonings. They have a light salty flavor and a crisp texture, suitable as a standalone snack or as a complement to dips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cracker chips are often used as a base for canapés and appetizers.
They originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to use leftover dough.
There are many flavor variants: cheese, barbecue, spicy, and herb-infused.
In some countries they are called “salted sticks” or “snack chips.”

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unlike sweet snacks, cracker chips contain almost no sugar, making them more suitable for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat flour provides slow‑release energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains vegetable oils
items.content: The oil used in baking supplies essential fatty acids.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Cracker chips contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt is added for flavor; those monitoring sodium intake should choose reduced‑salt versions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite their light texture, chips can be calorie‑dense due to oil; moderation is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cracker chips can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, paired with dip sauces, guacamole, cheese spreads, or added to salads for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to maintain crispness and prevent rancidity.
